Arrow convention

Where an arrow starts and ends, in three cases (decisions 53 to 55 of docs/DECISIONS.md; rules in docs/handoff/arrow-convention_2026-11-26.md). The arrows are drawn by the agent ink 0.4.0 without noise: the arrow in colour is the one the rule is about, a dot marks its start, the shaded area is the place the rule allows. L is a bond length.

An arrow drawn like a right one should give the step’s structure; a wrong one breaks one rule and can be read as another arrow. Answer on what you see in each attempt: the page does not show which attempts break a rule on purpose.

1. From a lone pair or a charge

  • The start lies in a direction at least 30° from each bond of the atom; it may face the target only inside that free sector.
  • Distance from the atom: 0.15 to 0.3 of a bond length, and at least 0.15 of a bond length from every bond line.
  • On a charged atom, a start at the charge sign is right (decision 55).

2. From or to a single bond

  • The start lies on the line, in the middle half of the bond (25 % to 75 %).
  • A short arrow (from a bond to one of its own atoms) starts on the bond and has a taller arc.
  • An end on an atom lies within 0.2 of a bond length of it, on a side clear of that atom’s bonds.

3. From or to a multiple bond

  • From a multiple bond to another atom: the start lies 55 % to 75 % of the way toward the atom that forms the new bond, and the arc bulges on that atom’s side.
  • A new single bond ends at the middle between the two atoms (45 % to 55 %) or on the receiving atom (within 0.2 of a bond length); both are right (decision 55), nothing in between.
  • An end on a bond that gains an order lies on the middle of its line (30 % to 70 %), never on one of its atoms.

Rules broken on purpose by the agent testers

In 20 % of the arrow attempts of the precise testers (john0002, john0003) and 40 % of those of the imprecise testers (john0004, john0005), exactly one arrow breaks exactly one of these rules; the other arrows follow the convention (decision 55). The rule is drawn among those that apply to the arrows of the step. The run record states it per attempt (convention); the review page does not show it.
